{{Short description|Educational mathematics technique}}
'''Skip counting''' is a mathematics technique taught as a kind of multiplication in [[reform mathematics]] textbooks such as [[Investigations in Numbers, Data, and Space|TERC]]. In older textbooks, this technique is called '''counting by twos''' (threes, fours, etc.).

In skip counting by twos, a person can count to 10 by only naming every other even number:  2, 4, 6, 8, 10.<ref name="titleSkip Counting">{{cite web |url=http://www.mathsisfun.com/numbers/skip-counting.html |title=Skip Counting |access-date=2008-02-22 }}</ref> Combining the base (two, in this example) with the number of groups (five, in this example) produces the standard multiplication equation:  two multiplied by five equals ten.
